description:
# Compliance ticket for opi-q5k.6

Source check: opi-q5k.6 (fuzzy.test.ts audit)

## Gap

Upstream tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/fuzzy.test.ts asserts, for an exact match, that the returned score is strictly negative (the consecutive-bonus invariant):

    it("exact match has good score", () => {
      const result = fuzzyMatch("test", "test");
      assert.strictEqual(result.matches, true);
      assert.ok(result.score < 0); // Should be negative due to consecutive bonuses
    });

Our apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/fuzzy_test.exs "exact match" test asserts only matches: true — it does not assert `score < 0`.

## Work

1. Add an assertion in `fuzzy_test.exs` under "match/2" confirming that an exact-string match returns a negative score (or equivalent: whatever sign convention `OctoPi.TUI.Fuzzy` uses, mirror the upstream invariant that exact/consecutive matches score *better* than any non-match boundary score, and that the magnitude is nonzero).
2. If the Elixir implementation does not return a negative score for exact match, determine whether that reflects a semantic divergence (e.g., our score convention is ascending/positive where lower is better); if so, document in a comment rather than force the sign.
3. **Re-comparison step (required)**: after the assertion lands, re-read tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/fuzzy.test.ts top-to-bottom and confirm every upstream `it(...)` block has an equivalent in fuzzy_test.exs. Post a final comment on this ticket with that re-comparison.
4. Close this ticket.

## Deps
Blocks opi-q5k.1 (acceptance gate).

comments.text: Done. fuzzy_test.exs now asserts score < 0.0 for exact match 'test'/'test'. Re-comparison: all 12 upstream it(...) blocks in tmp/pi-mono fuzzy.test.ts have Elixir equivalents (enumerated in opi-q5k.6 audit).
